summary: Wua Lai is Chiang Mai’s historic silversmith quarter south of the Old City. Visit the Wat Sri Suphan temple grounds and Lanna Craft Wisdom Museum for a daytime craft context, then return on Saturday evening for the Wua Lai Walking Street market. The district is a lived-in neighbourhood, not a single attraction with uniform opening hours.
whyGo: See metalwork as a continuing local craft tradition, with artisans and traditional tools presented at the Lanna Craft Wisdom Museum inside Wat Sri Suphan.
Browse silverwork and other local crafts, food and performances at the Saturday street market.
bestFor: Visitors interested in craft heritage, buying handmade work, or pairing a temple visit with an evening market.
An easy south-of-the-Old-City outing that can be done on foot from Chiang Mai Gate.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed live workshop at a set time: the museum describes demonstrations and hands-on repoussé, but does not publish a schedule, price or booking procedure.
You want a quiet visit: Wua Lai Road becomes busy during Saturday Walking Street.
duration: Allow about 1–2 hours for the museum, temple grounds and a short daytime neighbourhood walk (planning estimate); allow 2–3 hours for a Saturday market browse and meal. The market runs approximately 17:00–22:00.
cost: Walking Street admission is free. The temple museum’s visitor information says admission is free; donations and purchases are optional. Workshop prices and silver prices are not published, so confirm directly before committing.
hours: Wat Sri Suphan and the museum are listed as open daily 06:00–18:00. The Saturday Walking Street runs about 17:00–22:00. Individual silver shops and artisan studios may keep different hours; no district-wide daytime schedule is published.
bestTime: For craft displays and temple grounds, visit during the day before 18:00. For the street market, come on Saturday early evening; the temple foundation recommends arriving early for a more relaxed browse and better selection.
gettingThere: From Chiang Mai Gate, walk south along Wua Lai Road about 1 km to Wat Sri Suphan. A red songthaew, tuk-tuk or Grab can take you to the temple; walking is the simplest option from the south side of the Old City. Expect road closures and slower access during Saturday market hours.
booking: No booking is needed for the market or museum entry according to the temple foundation. For a hands-on craft session, contact Wat Sri Suphan in advance: its site lists +66 61 403 2815 and a contact form, but does not state workshop availability, fees or reservation terms.
accessibility: Accessibility details are not published. The market occupies a public street and may be crowded; ask the temple about step-free access and workshop arrangements. The Silver Ubosot has a religious access restriction: the temple says women are traditionally not permitted inside, though the exterior can be viewed.
practicalTips: Separate the daytime temple/museum visit from the Saturday market if you want to see both without rushing; the temple closes at 18:00, when the market is beginning.
Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered at the temple, and remove shoes before entering buildings.
Ask a seller about material, weight and workmanship before buying silver; no standard market price or independent hallmark guidance was found in the cited sources.
Treat a scheduled artisan demonstration as unconfirmed until the temple replies; the public site does not provide a timetable.
decemberNotes: December 2026 Saturday market dates fall on 5, 12, 19 and 26 December, subject to local changes. The recurring Saturday schedule is published, but no specific December 2026 market programme or special holiday hours were found. The market is outdoors and likely to be busier around the Christmas/New Year travel period; that is a planning assumption, not a published forecast.
uncertainties: The museum site gives free admission and open-daily information but does not specify separate museum hours, live demonstration times or whether the workshop runs every day.
Workshop fees, required advance notice, language options and current capacity are unpublished.
Opening hours of independent daytime silver workshops and shops vary and could not be verified as a group.
No accessibility statement for the museum or market route was located.
